A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAFE study. The full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original failure-detection experiments on LIBERO, SimplerEnv and a physical Franka robot, including benchmark comparisons, feature visualizations and detection-timing analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a physical OpenVLA/WidowX evaluation and experiments varying training-task count and feature source.

M1.justification: The proposed last-layer feature extraction, accumulated MLP scores and L1 objective, LSTM predictor and classification objective, and functional conformal thresholds are unchanged. The new feature-source experiments are ablations rather than revisions of the proposed SAFE procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds eight physical WidowX lifting and pick-and-place tasks evaluated with OpenVLA, extending real-world coverage beyond the original Franka experiments. This introduces new robot/environment conditions and objects while retaining the original simulation and Franka coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds predictors using DINOv2, CLIP and concatenated DINOv2+CLIP image features as comparisons against VLA features, with both MLP and LSTM heads. The comparator membership in the original benchmark comparisons, including RND, LogpZO and STAC, is retained.

E3.justification: The new WidowX protocol uses 532 rollouts and six seen/two unseen tasks. Appendix D adds controlled evaluations with 1, 3, 5 or 7 training tasks and fixed unseen tests, plus feature-source comparisons on the existing Franka rollouts. Original metrics and training budgets remain unchanged. Table 5's SimplerEnv 2/2 task split conflicts with the retained 3/1 description, so an actual split revision cannot be established.

E4.justification: New Appendix D systematically tests dependence on training-task count and whether VLA features outperform general image-encoder features. These address data requirements and representation choice beyond v1's feature-aggregation tuning, visualizations, conformal-prediction analysis and failure-timing studies, which are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-seed simulation and five-seed real-world averaging practices are retained. v2 Table 8 reproduces v1 Table 4's means and standard deviations. The added experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test or stated increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Original simulation and Franka benchmark scores are unchanged. v2 Figure 6 adds WidowX unseen-task ROC-AUC results of 88.42 for SAFE-MLP, 71.80 for SAFE-LSTM and 70.00 for Mahalanobis distance. Tables 6–7 add task-count and feature-source results; for example, Franka MLP ROC-AUC is 64.16 with VLA features versus 59.77 with CLIP. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, scoring functions, losses, conformal-band construction and associated assumptions are retained. New conceptual discussions introduce no substantive definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the comparative accuracy/timeliness claim from 'the best trade-off' to 'a favorable trade-off.' The multitask-generalization and state-of-the-art contributions remain unchanged, and the introduction still claims the best trade-off, making this a limited qualification.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of the new ablations and discussions distinguishing direct failure prediction from uncertainty and OOD proxies. Sections 6.4 and Appendices E–F expand deployment requirements, the rationale and trade-offs for last-layer features and offline calibration, and limitations of recovery or activation-steering extensions. The existing warning about conformal guarantees under task shift remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds the WidowX setup and task list, benchmark split counts, exact deployment measurements such as SAFE-LSTM's 2.3 million parameters and 0.73 ms inference time, and disclosure that most qualitative analyses use alpha = 0.15. The abstract now directs readers to code through the project webpage. Existing optimizer, hardware and hyperparameter-grid information is retained.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, covering predictive red teaming, intervention-based failure identification, automotive OOD detection, adaptive conformal inference and activation steering. The FAIL-Detect discussion now singles out LogpZO as its best method and describes RND as a strong baseline. SAFE's overall positioning as supervised multitask failure detection remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract, introduction, related work and results, adds a deployment-efficiency subsection, and expands the appendix into separate impact, experiment, results, ablation, discussion and future-work sections. The main narrative order and most retained technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method-overview Figure 2, expands the robot-setup illustration with WidowX, and adds WidowX columns to the real-world results display. New Tables 4–7 present tasks, benchmark statistics and ablations. Existing qualitative plots receive revised colors and captions, while retained figures and tables are resized, relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional physical robot evaluation and controlled ablations strengthen empirical support and help assess training-data requirements and the value of VLA features. The overview diagram and deployment details also improve clarity. These gains are tempered by Table 5's contradictory SimplerEnv split and unexplained Octo entry, and by missing dispersion estimates for the new WidowX results. Overall, v2 provides useful additional support with remaining reporting weaknesses.
